initial_plan.can_answer: yes: crash-record frequency per occurrence of each weekday describes how often a crash was reported on a typical calendar occurrence of that weekday, but does not measure risk or traffic-adjusted rates
initial_plan.metric: mean number of police-reported crash records per calendar occurrence of each weekday
initial_plan.denominator: number of dates in 2013-2025 on which each weekday occurs
initial_plan.population: crash records with crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive; calendar dates supply exposure denominators
initial_plan.grouping: day of week derived from crash_date, Monday through Sunday

data_check.facts: check_2.csv: 2,132,218 eligible records; each target year has observed dates from January 1 through December 31; zero source rows have NULL crash_date; zero rows use the checked sentinel dates; weekday is derivable for all eligible rows.
data_check.meaning_and_decisions: The date filter excludes no rows for a missing date within the target period; rows outside 2013-2025 are not in the planned population. All eligible rows are kept. crash_date is a DATE, so empty strings, unknown words, and impossible dates are not representable. No rows are reclassified or counted differently. Calendar-date denominator includes every date in the target interval, whether or not a crash was reported.

final_plan.can_answer: yes, as the mean number of police-reported crash records per calendar occurrence of each weekday
final_plan.metric: mean number of police-reported crash records per calendar occurrence of each weekday
final_plan.denominator: number of calendar dates in 2013-2025 inclusive on which that weekday occurs
final_plan.population: all crash records with crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive; denominator is all calendar dates in this same interval
final_plan.grouping: day of week derived from crash_date, Monday through Sunday
final_plan.limitations: The data check found no missing crash dates and full-year observed date endpoints in every target year. Calendar dates, not vehicle miles, traffic volume, or person-trips, form the denominator, so these are average reported-crash counts per weekday date and not crash risks.
